provenance.l: Apollo 14 Mission Report MSC-04112 (May 1971): Table 6-I, entry interface 215:47:45.3 at 400,000 ft, 36,170.2 ft/s (11,025 m/s); trajectory postflight evaluation MSC 04330 Table VII, flight-path angle -6.37 deg; Table A-II, command module weight at entry 12,703.5 lb (5,762 kg); section 11.3.1, landing 216:01:58 GET (21:05:00 GMT 9 February 1971), 0.62 n.mi from the target, USS New Orleans. Times are the Mission Report clock, not the Flight Journal clock (which runs 40 min 2.9 s ahead). Quote: "The command module landed February 9, 1971, at 2105 G.m.t. and remained in the stable I flotation attitude."

NASA SP-4029 Apollo chronology, "Entry, Splashdown, and Recovery" compilation (Apollo 7-17): entry interface velocity, flight-path angle, lift-to-drag ratio, range to target, maximum g, entry-to-splashdown duration, splashdown position and CM weight. Apollo 14 column: "Lift To Drag Ratio 0.280", "Range (n mi) 1,234" (1,234 n.mi = 2,285 km), "Maximum g 6.76", "Duration (sec) 852.8", "Velocity (ft/sec) 36,170.2", "Flight Path Angle -6.370", splashdown 27.02 S 172.67 W. No Apollo 14 entry postflight analysis was found online (MSC IN 71-FM-102 is cited in MSC 04330 but not on NTRS), so L/D and range are the compilation values (secondary); no first/second load-factor split is published. Model limit (US Standard Atmosphere 1976, 2026-11-25): with these inputs the model's first pulse is 6 g at 83 s (6.76 g flown), it dips to 2 g, second pulse 6.3 g; drogues 424 s (503 s flown, 8 min 23 s), splashdown 776 s (853 s flown). The larger pulse is within 10% of the flown maximum g; the entry runs short of the flown time, a limit of the fixed-bank planar guidance (on Apollo 11, the one flight with a published minimum, it lofts to 0.8 g between the pulses against the flown 0.48 g)

Apollo Flight Journal, Apollo 14 day 9 (clock 40:02.9 ahead of the Mission Report): "Shepard (onboard): 6.75" on the first pulse, drogues "216:36:12" (215:56:08 on the Mission Report clock), one main chute stayed fouled on the command module after splashdown
Apollo CM entry aero (L/D 0.3), drogue and main areas: the Apollo 8 profile (MSC-PA-R-69-1), same Block II command module
